title: Chapter 23. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VII: the ashtakaliya (the last part of the night, morning, day, evening)
html:
Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 23: the continuation of GPT section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" (GPT1 pp. 348–362, nos. 16–51): the Lord's words in sleep at the end of the night and His awakening; the morning in Shachi's house among the companions; the pastimes of the day — the Lord playfully takes away the companions' clothes, the meal on the bank of the Ganga; the walk through Navadvipa — old men, old women, the blind, the lame, the dandies and the merchants gaze at Him; the companions' longing at night as they wait for the dawn; two "table-of-contents" padas of the ashtakaliya (the eight parts of Gaura's day and night); the evening kirtanas — the Lord's dance in the guise of Rukmini and the dance in Srivasa's courtyard. The signatures in the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kiranas 1–4) and the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) were read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside the appendix): nos. 17, 52, 54 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 18 — Yadunatha Dasa (translated in chapter 13, no. 16); nos. 24, 25, 30, 32, 53 — Vasu Ghosha (no. 24 — chapter 12, no. 7; no. 25 = PK 1108 — chapter 5; no. 32 — chapter 5; no. 53 = PK 656 — chapter 9; no. 30 — the festival in the house of Narahari Thakura at Shrikhanda, signed Vasu); nos. 29, 41 — Narottama Dasa; no. 31 — Madhava (= PK 2638); nos. 33, 46 — Radhamohana; no. 44 — without the Narahari signature (= PK vol. 4); no. 45 — Vaishnava Dasa; no. 39 — a pada in nagari-bhava (assigned to the section of nagari padas). The padas on Gaura's night sleep (nos. 55–63, 65) go to the next chapter. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated with GPT2, the GCC (ed. 1947) and the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960); the PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya were checked. On the ashtakaliya as eternal lila and on the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22; on the motif of the women of Nadia, note 7. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "alasa abaśa pahum̐ rasika-śiromaṇi…" (GPT1 pp. 348–349, section 5.2, no. 16; GCC)

The last part of the night: the Lord, in the languor of half-sleep, speaks as in a dream words full of rasa: without the sight of Radharamana His life is burning; calling by name Gauridasa, Haridasa, Dhananjaya and dozens of companions, He asks them to sing of the deeds of the people of Vraja to quench the burning of His heart; in humility He says that enemies have subdued Him and He has taken a body in vain, and prays to be, birth after birth, a servant of the feet of the Lord of the gopis; having said this, He grows still again in sleep. Raga not stated. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.1

অলস অবশ পহুঁ রসিক-শিরোমণি কহত স্বপন সম রস রস বাত ।
রাধারমণ-দরশ-রস-বিরহিত জর জর জীউ জীউ জরি যাত ॥

alasa abaśa pahum̐ rasika-śiromaṇi kahata svapana sama rasa rasa bāta |
rādhāramaṇa-daraśa-rasa-birahita jara jara jīu jīu jari yāta ||

alasa — languid; abaśa — overcome; pahum̐ — the Lord; rasika-śiromaṇi — crown of the relishers of rasa; kahata — speaks; svapana sama — as in a dream; rasa rasa bāta — words full of rasa; rādhāramaṇa — Radharamana (Krishna); daraśa-rasa — the rasa of seeing; birahita — bereft of; jara jara — wasting away; jīu jīu — life, life; jari yāta — burns away

1.1Languid and overcome, my Lord, the crown of the relishers of rasa, speaks as in a dream words full of rasa: "Bereft of the rasa of seeing Radharamana, My life is wasting — My life is burning away.2

শুনহ গৌরী হরিদাস ধনঞ্জয় সঞ্জয় বিজয় মুকুন্দ মুরারি ।
মাধব বাসুদেব পুরুষোত্তম শ্রীধর কৃষ্ণদাস সুখকারী ॥

śunaha gaurī haridāsa dhanañjaya sañjaya bijaya mukunda murāri |
mādhaba bāsudeba puruṣottama śrīdhara kṛṣṇadāsa sukhakārī ||

śunaha — listen; gaurī — Gauri[dasa]; haridāsa, dhanañjaya, sañjaya, bijaya, mukunda, murāri — Haridasa, Dhananjaya, Sanjaya, Vijaya, Mukunda, Murari; mādhaba, bāsudeba, puruṣottama, śrīdhara — Madhava, Vasudeva, Purushottama, Shridhara; kṛṣṇadāsa — Krishnadasa; sukhakārī — giver of joy

1.2Listen, Gauri[dasa], Haridasa, Dhananjaya, Sanjaya, Vijaya, Mukunda, Murari,
Madhava, Vasudeva, Purushottama, Shridhara, Krishnadasa, giver of joy,

শ্রীনিধি মধুসূদন বক্রেশ্বর সত্যরাজ কবিচন্দ্র সুধীর ।
শঙ্কর গরুড় ভাগবত নন্দন চন্দ্রশেখর সারঙ্গ গভীর ॥

śrīnidhi madhusūdana bakreśvara satyarāja kabicandra sudhīra |
śaṅkara garuṛa bhāgabata nandana candraśekhara sāraṅga gabhīra ||

śrīnidhi, madhusūdana, bakreśvara, satyarāja — Shrinidhi, Madhusudana, Vakreshvara, Satyaraja; kabicandra sudhīra — wise Kavichandra; śaṅkara, garuṛa, bhāgabata, nandana, candraśekhara — Shankara, Garuda, Bhagavata, Nandana, Chandrashekhara; sāraṅga gabhīra — deep Saranga

1.3Shrinidhi, Madhusudana, Vakreshvara, Satyaraja, wise Kavichandra,
Shankara, Garuda, Bhagavata, Nandana, Chandrashekhara, deep Saranga,

শুক্লাম্বর যদুনাথ নকুল বনমালী মহেশ শ্রীনিধি গুণধাম ।
বিধি অতি সদয় সমুঝি মঝু অন্তর তুয়া সব সঙ্গ দেয়ল অবিরাম ॥

śuklāmbara yadunātha nakula banamālī maheśa śrīnidhi guṇadhāma |
bidhi ati sadaya samujhi majhu antara tuyā saba saṅga deyala abirāma ||

śuklāmbara, yadunātha, nakula, banamālī, maheśa, śrīnidhi — Shuklambara, Yadunatha, Nakula, Vanamali, Mahesha, Shrinidhi; guṇadhāma — abode of virtues; bidhi — the Creator; ati sadaya — most kind; samujhi — understanding; majhu antara — My heart; tuyā saba saṅga — all of you as companions; deyala — gave; abirāma — unceasingly

1.4Shuklambara, Yadunatha, Nakula, Vanamali, Mahesha, Shrinidhi, abode of virtues!
The Creator, most kind, understanding My heart, gave Me all of you as inseparable companions.

তাহে মানি মম বিনতি বাণী উহ ব্রজজন-চারু-চরিত-রসপূর ।
মধুর রাগ পরভাগ গাই ইহ দারুণ হৃদয়-তাপ করু দূর ॥

tāhe māni mama binati bāṇī uha brajajana-cāru-carita-rasapūra |
madhura rāga parabhāga gāi iha dāruṇa hṛdaya-tāpa karu dūra ||

tāhe — therefore; māni — accept; mama binati bāṇī — My humble request; uha — those; brajajana-cāru-carita — lovely deeds of the people of Vraja; rasa-pūra — full of rasa; madhura rāga — of sweet ragas; parabhāga — in their full beauty; gāi — singing; iha dāruṇa hṛdaya-tāpa — this cruel burning of the heart; karu dūra — remove

1.5So accept My humble request: those lovely deeds of the people of Vraja, full of rasa,
sing in all the beauty of sweet ragas — and quench this cruel burning of My heart.

মরমবাত বেকত কত করব এ প্রবল খলহ রিপু করল অধীন ।
ধরিনু দেহ বিফল কছু না বুঝলুঁ হোয়লুঁ প্রেম ভরাতি পথহীন ॥

maramabāta bekata kata karaba e prabala khalaha ripu karala adhīna |
dharinu deha biphala kachu nā bujhalum̐ hoyalum̐ prema bharāti pathahīna ||

marama-bāta — the secret of the heart; bekata kata karaba — how much shall I reveal; e prabala khalaha ripu — these mighty wicked enemies; karala adhīna — have subdued; dharinu deha — I took a body; biphala — in vain; kachu nā bujhalum̐ — I understood nothing; hoyalum̐ — I became; prema bharāti — in the bewilderment of prema (?); pathahīna — pathless

1.6How much shall I reveal the secret of My heart? These mighty wicked enemies have subdued Me; in vain I have taken a body — I have understood nothing, I have lost the way in the bewilderment of prema.

পুন কর জোড়ি কহিয়ে সুখ সঞে সভে পূরহ নিজজন-মনো-অভিলাষ ।
জনম জনম অবিরোধে হইয়ে জনি গোপী-পতিক-পদ-পঙ্কজ-দাস ॥

puna kara joṛi kahiye sukha sañe sabhe pūraha nijajana-mano-abhilāṣa |
janama janama abirodhe haiye jani gopī-patika-pada-paṅkaja-dāsa ||

puna — again; kara joṛi — with joined palms; kahiye — I say; sukha sañe — with joy; sabhe — all; pūraha — fulfil; nijajana-mano-abhilāṣa — the heart's desire of the One who is your own; janama janama — birth after birth; abirodhe — without hindrance; haiye jani — that I may be; gopī-patika — of the Lord of the gopis; pada-paṅkaja-dāsa — servant of the lotus feet

1.7Again, with joined palms, I say: all of you, with joy, fulfil the heart's desire of the One who is your own — that birth after birth, without hindrance, I may be a servant of the lotus feet of the Lord of the gopis."3

ঐছন বচন ভণত পুন কিঞ্চিত ঘুমে নীরব ভেল দ্বিজকুল-ভূপ ।
নরহরি ধন্দ ন বরণে শকত কছু সুরগণ-দুলহ সুচরিত অনুপ ॥

aichana bacana bhaṇata puna kiñcita ghume nīraba bhela dvijakula-bhūpa |
narahari dhanda na baraṇe śakata kachu suragaṇa-dulaha sucarita anupa ||

aichana bacana bhaṇata — having spoken such words; puna — again; kiñcita ghume — sinking a little into sleep; nīraba bhela — fell silent; dvijakula-bhūpa — the Lord of the twice-born; narahari dhanda — Narahari, bewildered; na baraṇe śakata kachu — cannot describe at all; suragaṇa-dulaha — rare even for the gods; sucarita anupa — the incomparable lovely deed

1.8Having spoken such words, the Lord of the twice-born, sinking for a little into sleep, again fell silent. Narahari, bewildered, cannot describe this incomparable lovely deed, rare even for the gods.

not know it** (new row NG-295). GCC — kirana 2 ("the pastimes on the bed" in the last part of the night), pada 25: after the awakening songs sung by the parrot (padas 14–23; chapter 22, nos. 17–26, note 35), the GCC says that Gaura, absorbed in rasa, heard a little of them (pada 24) — and the Lord speaks these words in His sleep. Variants: 1.1 GCC "rasamaya bāta" ("words full of rasa"; GPT "rasa rasa bāta"); 1.6 GCC "maramaka bāta", "hom̐yalu"; 1.7 GCC "jaga" for "jani". The name "Shrinidhi" stands twice in the list in all witnesses. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the ashtakaliya and the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22. for Him. The list names the Lord's companions in Navadvipa, mostly known from the biographies: Gauridasa Pandita (in the GCC "gauri"), Haridasa Thakura, Dhananjaya, Sanjaya, Vijaya Dasa, Mukunda Datta, Murari Gupta, Shridhara, Vakreshvara Pandita, Satyaraja Khan, Garuda Pandita, Nandana Acharya, Chandrashekhara Acharya, Shuklambara Brahmachari, Nakula Brahmachari, Vanamali and others. "enemies" (lust, anger and the rest), but, relishing the mood of a bhakta, speaks of Himself as a fallen soul — cf. His words "there is not a trace of love for Krishna in Me" (CC Madhya 2.42), the prayer "birth after birth, causeless devotion to You" (Shikshashtaka, CC Antya 20.29) and the verse "a servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of the Lord of the gopis" (CC Madhya 13.80). The reading "prema bharāti" (GCC "premabharāti") is unclear; understood as "prema-bhrānti", "the bewilderment of prema".

2. Narahari — "śuti rahum̐ sundara gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 pp. 349–350, no. 19; GCC)

Dawn: the beautiful young Gaura is still asleep; the companions read prose and verse, sing songs about Him to instruments, compose verses, loudly recite the names, weep in humility; the cows low, calling their calves — and the Lord, hearing them, wakes, stretches, yawns, leaves the chamber and asks for the hobbling rope, calling Gauridasa and the others by their former names. Raga not stated. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.4

শুতি রহুঁ সুন্দর গৌরকিশোর ।
দিনকর পূরুব দিশাগত গতি পর জাগত জন যামিনী ভেল ভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

śuti rahum̐ sundara gaurakiśora |
dinakara pūruba diśāgata gati para jāgata jana yāminī bhela bhora || dhru ||

śuti rahum̐ — still lies; sundara gaura-kiśora — the beautiful young Gaura; dinakara — the sun; pūruba diśāgata gati para — on its way toward the east; jāgata jana — people wake; yāminī bhela bhora — the night is over

2.1The beautiful young Gaura still lies [asleep].
The sun is already on its way to the east, people are waking — the night is over.

কোই মধুরতর গদ্য পদ্য করু পাঠ নিরত পরমাদ্ভুত রীত ।
কোই যন্ত্রকুল মিলিত সুগাওত পহুঁক প্রীতি-চরিতময় গীত ॥

koi madhuratara gadya padya karu pāṭha nirata paramādbhuta rīta |
koi yantrakula milita sugāota pahum̐ka prīti-caritamaya gīta ||

koi — someone; madhuratara gadya padya — the sweetest prose and verse; karu pāṭha — reads; nirata — wholly absorbed; paramādbhuta rīta — a wondrous thing; yantrakula milita — with many instruments; sugāota — sings beautifully; pahum̐ka prīti-caritamaya gīta — songs of the Lord's loving deeds

2.2Someone reads the sweetest prose and verse, wholly absorbed in it — a wondrous thing!
Someone, to the sound of many instruments, beautifully sings songs of the Lord's loving deeds.

কোই রুচির রচনা করু নিয়মিত উচরত নাম উচ্চ করি কোয় ।
কোই দৈন্যহত মাতি ভক্তিরসে শরদ ঘটা পটতর নাহি হোয় ॥

koi rucira racanā karu niyamita ucarata nāma ucca kari koya |
koi dainyahata māti bhaktirase śarada ghaṭā paṭatara nāhi hoya ||

koi — someone; rucira racanā karu — composes lovely verses; niyamita — by vow; ucarata nāma ucca kari — loudly recites the names; dainya-hata — struck down by humility; māti bhakti-rase — drunk with the rasa of bhakti; śarada ghaṭā — an autumn downpour (?); paṭantara nāhi hoya — does not compare

2.3Someone composes lovely verses, someone by vow loudly recites the names, someone, struck down by humility, is drunk with the rasa of bhakti — not even an autumn downpour compares with it.

গরজত গাভী লেই ভর আতুর নিজ নিজ বতস পিয়াঅন লাগি ।
তাকর শবদ শুনত অতি তুরিতহি শেজ উপরি পহুঁ বৈঠল জাগি ॥

garajata gābhī lei bhara ātura nija nija batasa piyāana lāgi |
tākara śabada śunata ati turitahi śeja upari pahum̐ baiṭhala jāgi ||

garajata gābhī — the cows low; lei bhara ātura — distressed by the weight [of their udders]; nija nija batasa piyāana lāgi — to give milk to their own calves; tākara śabada śunata — hearing their call; ati turita-hi — at once; śeja upari — on the bed; pahum̐ baiṭhala jāgi — the Lord woke and sat up

2.4The cows low, distressed by the weight of their udders — they must give milk to their calves; hearing their call, the Lord at once woke and sat up on the bed.

পুন কর মোড়ি চারু করযুগে যুগ লোচন ঝাঁপি জিম্ভায়ত থোর ।
মন্দির তেজি চলত চিত চঞ্চল মাগত ঘন ঘন ছাঁদন-ডোর ॥

puna kara moṛi cāru karayuge yuga locana jhām̐pi jimbhāyata thora |
mandira teji calata cita cañcala māgata ghana ghana chām̐dana-ḍora ||

puna — then; kara moṛi — stretching; cāru karayuge — with His lovely palms; yuga locana jhām̐pi — covering both eyes; jimbhāyata thora — yawned a little; mandira teji — leaving the chamber; calata — goes; cita cañcala — with an eager heart; māgata ghana ghana — asks again and again; chām̐dana-ḍora — the hobbling rope

2.5Then He stretched, covered both eyes with His lovely palms, yawned a little, left the chamber and goes with an eager heart, asking again and again for the hobbling rope.5

নিরখি গৌরীদাসাদিক জনে জনে পূরুব নাম লই বদত উলাস ।
নরহরি ভণ সুচরিত্র চিত্র ইহ ঘুম ঘোর কি এ প্রেমবিলাস ॥

nirakhi gaurīdāsādika jane jane pūruba nāma lai badata ulāsa |
narahari bhaṇa sucaritra citra iha ghuma ghora ki e premabilāsa ||

nirakhi — seeing; gaurīdāsādika — Gauridasa and the others; jane jane — each one; pūruba nāma lai — by his former name; badata ulāsa — calls joyfully; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; sucaritra citra iha — wondrous is this lovely deed; ghuma ghora — deep sleep; ki e prema-bilāsa — or is it a play of prema

2.6Seeing Gauridasa and the others, He joyfully calls each by his former name.
Narahari says: wondrous is this lovely deed — is it deep sleep, or a play of prema?

awakening"), pada 10. Variants: 2.2 GCC "kou" for "koi" (and so on); 2.3 GCC "śabda ghaṭāpaṭatara nāhi hoya" for "śarada ghaṭā paṭatara…" — the end of the line is unclear in both readings, the translation is tentative ("not even the roar of autumn clouds compares with it" by the GCC); 2.4 GPT1 "rata sapiyā ana" — a misprint, corrected by the GCC "batasa piyāana" ("to give milk to the calves"); 2.5 GCC "puna tanu moṛi" ("stretched His body"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. cowherd boy of Vraja: He hurries to the cows and calls the companions by their "former names", their names in Krishna's lila (thus Gauridasa Pandita is Subala, Krishna's friend, according to Kavi Karnapura's Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika). Here too the Lord's sleep is absorption in the lilas of Vraja (note 36 of chapter 22).

3. Narahari — "pekhaha gauracandra aparūpa…" (GPT1 p. 350, no. 20; GCC)

Morning: Gaurachandra, still drowsy, sits on a jewelled seat; the radiance of His body fills the three worlds and rises in the hearts of His own; His smile is lovelier than a forest of lotuses, His sleepy eyes are reddish; jasmine flowers fall from His loosened hair like stars to the earth. Raga not stated. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.6

পেখহ গৌরচন্দ্র অপরূপ ।
ঝলমল ললিত সুরতন পীঠ পরি বিলসত নিরুপম মনমথ-ভূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

pekhaha gauracandra aparūpa |
jhalamala lalita suratana pīṭha pari bilasata nirupama manamatha-bhūpa || dhru ||

pekhaha — behold; gauracandra aparūpa — the wondrous Gaurachandra; jhalamala — gleaming; lalita — lovely; suratana pīṭha pari — on a seat of jewels; bilasata — sits resplendent; nirupama — incomparable; manamatha-bhūpa — king Kamadeva

3.1Behold the wondrous Gaurachandra!
On a gleaming lovely seat of jewels sits the incomparable king Kamadeva.

সুরগিরি-শিখর-দরপ-হর বরতনু তেজ প্রবল ত্রিভুবন ভরি পূর ।
নিজজন-হৃদয় উদয় করু অবিরত রবি শশী কোটি গরব করু চূর ॥

suragiri-śikhara-darapa-hara baratanu teja prabala tribhubana bhari pūra |
